summary: velora-kit fetches remote JavaScript from a bare-IP endpoint and executes it with full Node privileges
details: index.js exports a getPlugin function that fetches JSON from a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint (https://31.97.137.157:45000/icons/116) and passes a field from the response body to the Function constructor, executing the returned code in the installer's Node.js process with require, module, process, and Buffer injected. The destination URL is assembled by concatenating split string constants (protocol, separator, domain, path) and wrapped in helpers referring to an icon/CDN cover story that has no relation to the actual endpoint. The package's dependency set (@primno/dpapi, better-sqlite3, node-machine-id) contradicts the README's claim of a lightweight zero-dependency utility and matches the tooling profile of credential-theft droppers. The operator of 31.97.137.157:45000 controls the code that runs on any host that invokes the exported function.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
